newsitem.title: USA: Wang looks for $250-$300 mln from Kodak - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Wang looks for $250-$300 mln from Kodak - analysts.

text.p: Analysts said the reported $250 million to $300 million sale price that Wang Laboratories Inc is seeking from Eastman Kodak for its imaging unit "is a pretty good price for Wang."
"And it's a very attractive business for Kodak," said Smtih Barney analyst David Zimm. "It has very high gross margins."

The Bellica, Mass.-based Wang unit, which employs about 300 people, had revenues of $50 million in fiscal 1995 and Prudential Securities Research analyst Alex Henderson is estimating revenues for fiscal 1996 will be $75 million.
"This is a case where Kodak wants to buy, not necessarily where Wang wants to sell. So they will probably hold out for that $250 million-$300 million range," Henderson said.

Rochester, N.Y.-based Kodak, which reported sales of $4.117 billion in the second quarter, has seen a weakening in its microfilm/microfiche business, Henderson said. The two companies have had a strategic alliance since last year, "And now, Kodak sees that it is really working out, so it's time to really pony up...it will give them something else to sell."
A Kodak spokesman refused to comment on the talks, saying "We never comment on speculation," but a Wang spokeswoman confirmed the two sides were in negotiations.

"This is not a risk-free transaction," Henderson said, calling Kodak a chemistry company that was looking to buy a software firm. "It wouldn't be the first time that a young, vibrant, high-energy company ran into a stodgy Fortune 500 company and failed."
Imaging software is a $2.5 billion market in the United States and growing, Henderson said.
Wang, which has a $1 billion net operating loss "and won't be paying any taxes for the next five years at least," noted Henderson, has been in an acquisiton mode.
In July, Wang bought I-NET, a Bethesda, Md-based company that builds and services computer networks for $167 million cash.
Both Zimm and Henderson expected Wang's appetite for acquisition to grow if the sale of its imaging unit goes through. "Net-net, they're in the acquisition mode," Zimm said.
